edges.effect_quant: Systematic reviews and randomized trials consistently show better chewing function with implant-supported mandibular prostheses than with conventional complete dentures alone. Review-level evidence reports superior masticatory performance and chewing satisfaction with implant-retained overdentures, and randomized trials in edentulous older adults show measurable gains after implant conversion.
edges.population: edentulous adults receiving implant-supported mandibular overdentures or other long-term implant-supported oral rehabilitation
edges.mechanism: Implant support improves denture stability, retention, and force transmission during mastication, reducing prosthesis movement and allowing more efficient comminution of food than unstable conventional dentures.
edges.summary: This is a solid oral-function edge. Compared with conventional complete dentures, implant-supported mandibular rehabilitation usually improves chewing quality and masticatory performance in edentulous adults.
edges.caveats: The strongest evidence comes from edentulous mandibular overdenture studies rather than every possible implant restoration. Benefit depends on baseline denture instability, implant success, prosthetic design, and patient adaptation over time.

evidence.citation: Kutkut A et al 2018 J Prosthodont Res
evidence.notes: A systematic review of studies comparing conventional complete denture and implant retained overdenture.

evidence.citation: Passia N et al 2017 J Dent
evidence.notes: Single mandibular implant study (SMIS) - masticatory performance - results from a randomized clinical trial using two different loading protocols.

evidence.citation: Garrett NR et al 1998 J Prosthet Dent
evidence.notes: A randomized clinical trial comparing the efficacy of mandibular implant-supported overdentures and conventional dentures in diabetic patients. Part II. Comparisons of masticatory performance.
